FR-001.title: Record each repository's last successfully indexed revision, only after the ingest commits

FR-002.title: At the recorded revision with no differing working tree, report already up to date and change nothing

FR-003.title: Determine added, changed, renamed and removed files by comparing the working tree against the last indexed revision

FR-004.title: Re-parse and re-embed only added, changed and renamed files; never rewrite unchanged files' symbols

FR-005.title: Remove every stored file, symbol and chunk of removed, renamed-away or newly skipped paths

FR-006.title: Incremental index equals what a full ingest of the same tree would produce

FR-007.title: Apply an incremental ingest in one transaction; failure keeps previous index and revision

FR-008.title: Summary reports added, changed, removed and unchanged file counts

FR-009.title: ccctx ingest <name> --full discards and rebuilds the repository's index

FR-010.title: Unknown or missing last indexed revision: say so and rebuild in full

FR-011.title: Up-to-date message tells the developer --full re-indexes anyway

FR-012.title: Keep read-only git, no code execution, concurrent-ingest refusal and the structured log record

expectations: detecting chunking-rule or skip-setting changes automatically (use --full)
watching repositories or re-indexing on a schedule
exposing ingest through the MCP server
context: area: src/golestan_code_mcp/schema.py (migrations; ccctx_repos gains last indexed revision)
constraint: git read-only with fsmonitor and hooks disabled; indexed code never executed
constraint: hybrid index syncs on commit, so re-embedding happens only for inserted rows
intent: Make re-ingest do only the work the changes since the last indexed revision require, purge deleted code, and offer --full

decisions.decision: Record indexed_commit, indexed_dirty, indexed_at on ccctx_repos (migration 5), written inside the index transaction
decisions.why: the locked repo row moves only if the index commits; NULL means rebuild in full
decisions.rejected: max(commit_sha) over symbols, a separate runs table

decisions.decision: git names candidates (diff --no-renames vs indexed commit, untracked, vanished stored paths, everything after a dirty ingest); content sha256 decides added/changed/removed/unchanged
decisions.why: reads only what changed yet stays exact for reverted edits, already-indexed dirty edits and new skip-rule hits
decisions.rejected: hashing every file each run; git diff alone

decisions.decision: Up to date = HEAD equals indexed_commit and empty change set; no separate fast path
decisions.why: one rule; a clean tree costs a few git calls and two queries
decisions.rejected: a git-status-only shortcut that cannot see untracked or reverted files

decisions.decision: Changed files are deleted and re-inserted; deletes cascade to symbols and the hybrid index syncs on commit
decisions.why: unique (repo_id, path) plus cascade make it the shortest correct path; only new rows are embedded
the request says leave correct rows alone; equality with --full is checked excluding commit_sha
decisions.rejected: restamping every symbol with the new revision

decisions.decision: --full is the only override, also how a user insists on an up-to-date repo
decisions.why: a second flag would do the same thing

decisions.decision: Changed files are updated in place and keep every symbol whose (name, kind, content hash) still occurs, updating only its lines and commit_sha
decisions.why: measured: the 40 files changed over flask's last 20 commits hold 658 symbols but only 140 changed; re-inserting whole files took 78% of a full rebuild. Updates and deletes cost nothing at commit, only inserts are embedded
decisions.rejected: delete and re-insert each changed file (the plan's first design)

decisions.decision: Lock the repository row first and read the revision and stored hashes under it; an up-to-date run rolls back
decisions.why: a concurrent ingest cannot make the change set stale, and the existing nowait refusal covers every mode

decisions.decision: Kept the skip rules and chunking unchanged
decisions.why: the requested --full check compares counts with the original ingest; changing what is indexed would break that and needs its own step

plan.summary: Plan, research, data model and CLI/schema contracts for incremental re-indexing in ingest.py, schema.py and cli.py
plan.key_finding: git diff against the last commit alone is wrong after a dirty ingest; an indexed_dirty flag plus content hashes keeps the change set exact

tasks.summary: 14 tasks: Foundational (3 fail-first test tasks, then schema, ingest, cli, green run), 4 sequential live-verification story phases on flask, Polish (README, contracts, full suite)

approach: Migration 5 records the last indexed revision on each repository. Git diff against it, plus untracked and vanished paths, names candidates; content hashes classify them; only added and changed files are parsed and inserted, removed and changed rows are deleted with cascade, all in one locked transaction. --full, a NULL revision or a missing commit run today's full replace.

concerns.note: SC-002 as written is not met: 17% of flask's files changed over HEAD~20 (target under 10%), and the incremental run takes 64% of a full rebuild on the same tree (52% of the first ingest), not under half. The user's own bar, a handful of files and noticeably faster, holds. 53% of the re-embedded text is uv.lock windows and 14% CHANGES.rst: a line inserted near the top shifts every 60-line window after it. Skipping lockfiles or content-defined windows would fix it, both need --full and change counts.

A full flask ingest now takes 650-680s, not the 125s step 4 measured: the hybrid index embeds on commit under the Free edition's CPU resource manager (resmgr:cpu quantum). README's 125.4s sample is stale.
A class symbol contains its methods, so editing one method re-embeds the whole class (Flask is 61k characters).
